rule: Designate a page as **key-step** when it introduces or carries a central derivation, proof transition, or result whose omission or distortion would break the explanatory chain. Every other page is not key-step.

pages.reason: Gives the historical setting (the Schonhage-Strassen n log n conjecture and the Harvey-van der Hoeven bound) and derives nothing. Leaving it out costs the reader context, but the chain of argument stays intact.
Defines the ring C[y]/(y^r+1), where powers of y act as signed coefficient shifts. The pages that use this ring do the derivations; this page only provides the concept.
Defines the disk-grid number format and the truncation Q_p with its standard error and norm facts. The error analyses rely on it, but it carries no step of the argument.
Recalls the known O(N log N) multiplier, which is used only as a black-box subroutine on short operands. It is standard material and derives nothing here.
Defines arrays, addresses, address fields and logical volume on tapes. It is the vocabulary for the tape lemmas and carries no derivation of its own.

States the standard linear-time tape scans (digit permutation, split and merge, row dealing) and derives no sub-steps. It supports the recursive procedures without carrying any part of the power saving.

States the O(V) controlled cyclic shift, done by splitting each fiber at the offset and merging the pieces in opposite order, with no derived sub-steps. The linear cost of the triangular shear factors and the CRT map depends on it, which makes the call close, but it is an elementary supporting lemma and carries no step of the chain.
Recalls standard material on rank, subspaces, bilinear forms and orthogonal complements, including over F_2. The label and shear pages use it, but it carries no step of the argument.

Derives the fixed linear network (S4.1.1-S4.1.10): its eight-row schedule cancels the old scratch values, achieves y <- y+x, chains three stages into the signed exchange (X,Y) -> (-Y,X), and counts the wires W. Both fast tape procedures run on this network, so a gap here breaks the recursion that produces the power saving.

Derives the lower-triangular (Bruhat) factorization A = E1 Pi E2, which shows that a rank-a shear costs exactly a field interchanges plus O(V), and that three shears give an interchange (S4.5.1.x). This rank-equals-cost transition is what lets the edge ranks s of the bit network become the number of recursive calls.

Derives the frame invariant: the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, so all intermediate frames cancel and each edge pays only D_v D_u^{-1} (S4.2.1-S4.2.2). Without this transition, edge costs could not be chosen freely as cheap rank changes, and the recursion would not be justified.

Derives the nested subspace labels from 3-element subsets, the loss ratios 100/539 and 101/539, and the total edge ranks s_b < W_b m and s_c < W_c m (S4.3.1-S4.3.7). This strict inequality is the source of the power saving, so a distortion here breaks the whole result.

Assembles network, frames and labels into the recursion and derives s/W < m^tau with tau = 1-2^-50 from the relative rank deficits (S4.4). This turns the rank saving into a cost exponent below one for both tape procedures, a central transition of the chain.

Derives the first tape procedure: the power-width interchange through the bit network, the recurrence F_k = O(e^tau), the tape scheduling, and the extension to arbitrary-width interchanges in O(V u^tau) (S4.5.2-S4.5.3). It removes the log-factor cost of address rearrangement, one of the two savings the main theorem needs.

Derives the packed XOR via eight cyclic shifts, the exceptional-address repair and its union bound, giving binary basis changes in O(V((eK)^tau+1)) (S4.6.2.x). It is a technical lemma deep inside the butterfly-layer recursion, which makes the call close, but without it the basis changes between C-layers lose their sublinear cost and the second tape procedure fails.

Derives signed Kronecker substitution: two's-complement packing, extraction of centered residues by induction, negacyclic wrap and truncation, giving the pointwise ring products in O(rp log(rp)) (S5.3.x). The technique is a standard adaptation, which makes the call close, but the ring convolution and the packed-product cost row cannot do without it.
Defines cyclic convolution as the product in the group algebra. Many steps use the concept, but this page derives nothing.

Derives the opening reduction of the chain: the integer product is a digit convolution with degree below S and coefficients below 2^{3b}, so there is no wraparound (S8.2.1-S8.2.3). The estimates are elementary, which makes the call close, but without this transition nothing connects the convolution to the integer product.

Derives the twist x_d -> zeta y and the wrap check, which convert the cyclic power-of-two convolution into the negacyclic ring convolution (M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(...) = (f*g)/T) together with its computed version (S8.4.x). This is a standard device, which makes the call close, but it is the link between the chirp convolution and the ring convolution in the reduction chain.

Derives the propagation of the final error through the pointwise product, the opposite transform and the rescalings to below 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2, then the rounding and the carry invariant (S8.8.1-S8.8.10). This step turns approximate transforms into the exact 2n-bit product, so an error here breaks the correctness of the theorem.
Recalls the normalized DFT, its inverse and the convolution theorem. This is standard background used by the transform pages, and it carries no step.
Defines the tensor-product transform on several axes. It is a supporting concept with no derivation of its own.
Defines the two-point butterfly H_0 and the decimation-in-frequency pairing. The synthetic transform and fast-layer pages derive what uses it, and this page carries no step.

Derives the transform over C[y]/(y^r+1) with omega_t = y^{2r/t}: the contraction property, inversion by character cancellation, the decimation-in-frequency recursion, the bit-reversed retained order consumed by the opposite transform, and multi-axis rounds (S5.1.1-S5.1.9). This is where roots of unity become exact signed shifts, which is central to the arithmetic side of the saving.

Derives the permuted chirp identity QF_t u = conj(a)(a*(conj(a) u))/T by comparing coefficients (S7.1.1-S7.1.5). It is a classical identity, which makes the call close, but its permuted form is what lets Q be absorbed without a sort, and permutation cancellation depends on it.

Derives the kernel identities (H_0 = b S C S, C^{-1} = -iZCZ), the coordinate form of edge changes via P_M, the s_c child layers on f axes, and H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D (S4.6.1.1-S4.6.1.8). This transition is what makes the complex network compute a butterfly layer recursively.

Derives the second tape procedure: the batched recurrence solving to O(V d^{lambda'}), the bit-growth bound Delta = o(p) for exact evaluation, and the single-truncation proposition with error < sqrt2 2^{-p} (S4.6.3-S4.6.5). It removes the log-factor cost of butterfly layers, the second saving the main theorem needs.

Derives the transform layout and its cost through chunk exchanges and fast layers, and the convolution error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} with total cost O(Tp[dK + pK^{tau-1} + l d^{lambda'} + log(rp)]) (S5.2, S5.4). Several of the dominant cost rows come from this page, which is the main computational engine of the chain.

Derives Gaussian resampling with both permutations kept inside the formula, RF_s = 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A, along with its contractions, errors and costs, and the tensor interface (S6.1, S6.2). Keeping the permutations avoids the two O(tp log t) sorts, so this central transition is needed both for the prime-to-power-of-two reduction and for the cost bound.

Derives RF_s^+ R = F_s^+ and the cancellation RF^+[(RFu)(RFv)] = (u*v)/S^2 (S7.2-S7.3). This proves that the retained permutations never need to be executed and still yield the true convolution, a central correctness transition.

Derives that the Agarwal-Cooley map Phi is a convolution-preserving isomorphism, its coordinate formula, and its implementation by triangular controlled shifts in O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) (S8.3.1-S8.3.7). The map is standard, which makes the call close, but the chain needs this sort-free transition from one cyclic axis to distinct prime axes, and it supplies a cost row.

Fixes the exponents and sizes and derives that suitable primes exist, that T/2 < S < T, that alpha^4 theta_i > p and that gamma <= b/4 (S8.1.1-S8.1.13). It is mostly parameter verification, which makes the call close, but the resampling hypotheses, the no-wraparound bound and the value of kappa all rest on it.

Assembles the reduction chain into the algorithm and derives the chirp and source-transform procedures, the six algorithm steps with their two scalings by S, and the error budget E_s = 9 2^gamma TL (S8.5-S8.7). It is the main transition from the components to an exact product, and the exact-recovery bound depends on its error budget.

Derives the seven normalized cost exponents, their margins with minimum 2^-181 = 2 kappa, the justification of each row and the total O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) (S9.1-S9.4). This final accounting produces the theorem's bound, so a distortion here breaks the result.

States the main result that every step of the chain serves, the O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) multitape multiplier, and lays out how the reductions and the two tape savings combine. Without it the explanatory chain has no endpoint.
